title: Rabbi Ami bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Ashi’s father-in-law, as Hyman quotes Chullin 111a: “Rav Ashi came to the house of Rav Ami bar Abba, his father-in-law; he saw his son,” etc. According to Dikdukei Soferim this is the reading in Beitzah 29a, and so it is in the She’iltot, Emor. He is mentioned in Nedarim 32a and Niddah 20a. In the Rif on Shabbat, beginning of chapter 15: “Rabbi Ami bar Abba said that Rav Ashi said: It is forbidden to walk on grass on Shabbat.” But the reading Hyman uses in Eruvin 100b is “Rami bar Amma said that Rav Assi said,” which Hyman prefers.

notes.text: The supplied Eruvin reading is Rami bar Amma (אמא), now preserved rather than normalized to Abba. Hyman’s preferred reading is distinct from the earlier Rif form. The father-in-law relationship remains explicit.

Hyman quotes Ami bar Abba as Rav Ashi’s father-in-law, while the consulted Chullin 111a–b reads Rami bar Abba. His supplied Eruvin reading is Rami bar Amma; the consulted Eruvin 100b reads Rami bar Abba in Rav Assi’s name. These occurrence-specific forms are retained separately. The exact Dikdukei Soferim, She’iltot and Rif readings remain Hyman’s reports.
